faq.a: Saifullah is associated with the Arabic form سَيْفُ اللَّه, whose core sense is saifullah; sword of god.

faq.q: What is the origin of Saifullah?
faq.a: Saifullah is associated with Arabic. Saifullah is Arabic سَيْفُ اللَّه (Sayf Allāh), meaning 'sword of God'.
Yes — the underlying form سَيْفُ اللَّه is Arabic.
Saifullah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Saifullah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Saif Allāh is a compound of Arabic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Saifullah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Saifullah is rendered سیف اللہ and carries the sense سیف اللہ، اللہ کی تلوار.

faq.q: What does Saifullah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Saifullah is rendered سیف‌الله and carries the sense سیف‌الله، شمشیر خدا.
A romanized syllable approximation is sai-ful-lah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Saifullah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Saifullah, saifullah. Script forms are سَيْفُ اللَّه, سیف الله, سیف اللہ, سیف‌الله, सैफ़ुल्लाह.

faq.q: Is Saifullah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
